nodes.title: H3 Characters — custom performer + wardrobe

widgets_values:
# H3 Music Video - masked audio, written locally by Ollama

The song is the clock. The writer cuts it into 5-15 s pieces on the music (timed
lyrics make cuts land before a line), writes one H3 scene per piece, and emits
matching lists - `scenes`, `lengths`, `audio_segments`, `clip_starts` - that the
video node renders one clip at a time.

**Masked audio** is what makes the lip-sync work: each clip's real slice of the
song is encoded and written straight into the H3 audio latent with the mask held
at 0, so the model generates picture against a frozen, real vocal instead of being
asked politely to sync. That is why the song is *not* wired to `ref_audio`.

**What is different here:** the scenes are written by a local model. The **Ollama
backend** node overrides the writer's `model` dropdown - the Claude Code CLI is
never called, no API key is needed, nothing leaves this machine. The model is multimodal, so the performer photo reaches it as well.

**Output:** every piece is decoded and saved as its own file by H3 Save Clip,
carrying its original slice of the song. Stitch them externally, or add
**H3 Scenes Join** with `replace_audio` = the LoadAudio output for one file with
the full mix.

**Seed:** the writer's seed is -1 (randomize) - every queue writes a brand-new
video. Set a fixed number to re-render the same scenes.


**What H3 listens to - Voice Over Music.** The audio in H3's latent is not the song itself but a mix made for the model: AudioSeparation's **Vocals** on top at full level, **Drums + Bass + Other** summed **-9 dB** under them and ducked a further **-6 dB** only while the voice sounds. The mouth follows the voice, the picture moves on the real beat, and no word gets buried (the plain song buried consonants; the bare vocal stem had no beat to cut on). `music_db` is the dial: -3 is nearly the full song, -18 a whisper of beat. The original song still goes to the output.

**Beats.** Sound Events (hits, drops, stops) → **Beat Grid** (the tempo and every beat, phase-fitted to the hits) → **Cut Plan** (the scenes, cut on the music) → the writer's `cut_plan` and `sound_events`. Every piece's brief then lists its `[beat]` offsets and its `[+start ->+land ->+settle s]` moments, and the scene is staged on them - the hit sentences are written ON TOP of the piece's picture budget, never instead of it.

**Clips land one by one.** The sampler and Save Clip are one node here - **Sampler + Save Clip** - so every scene is sampled, decoded, muxed with its slice of the song and written to `output/` BEFORE the next scene starts sampling. Watch the folder fill up during the run; a crash late in the run keeps everything already saved. (Two separate nodes would sample every scene first and only then start saving.)

nodes.title: H3 Music Video Writer - Ref2VA (vision model)
Masked-audio lip-sync
widgets_values:
**Masked-audio music video** - the strongest lip-sync H3 can do.

Each clip's exact slice of the song is encoded with the audio VAE and written straight into the H3 audio latent, protected from denoising (mask 0). The video is generated against the real, frozen vocal - lip-sync is enforced by the model, not requested by the prompt.

- The song is **not** connected to `ref_audio` (that is on purpose).
- The **vocal stem** (AudioSeparation) is injected so instruments don't mask the voice; the final soundtrack is still the full mix via Scenes Join `replace_audio`.
- The writer's `audio_mode` is set to *Masked latent*, so the prompts reference the protected master-song audio instead of `<Audio 1>`.
- `clip_starts` from the writer gives every clip its exact offset in the master song.

Needs audio-separation-nodes-comfyui (the masked-audio node is this pack's own H3 Masked Song Latent).

nodes.title: Ollama setup
widgets_values:
# Ollama setup - read this first

The whole video is written by **ollama:qwen3.8:27b** on this machine. Nothing is sent anywhere.

```
ollama pull qwen3.8:27b
ollama serve
```

Then reload the ComfyUI page so the backend node can see the model.

## num_ctx is the setting that matters

The H3 system prompt is **9k tokens** (text-only) to **15k tokens** (with reference
images) before your song, cast and lyrics are added. Ollama picks its own context
from free VRAM - as little as 4k - and **silently truncates** everything past it,
starting with the rules the model is supposed to follow. The result is not an
error, it is a bad prompt.

The **Ollama backend** node sets `num_ctx` explicitly (32768 here). Press
**📏 Show 1024 tokens** on that node to see what a token actually is, what an H3
run spends, and how much context fits in this machine's VRAM and RAM.

## The other two settings

- **thinking = off.** qwen3.8 reasons before answering by default. The H3 rules are
  already in the system prompt, so the reasoning is pure wall-clock cost. Any
  `<think>` block that does arrive is stripped before parsing either way.
- **scenes_per_call = 2, parallel_chunks = off.** One local model, one GPU: four
  concurrent chunks just queue behind each other. Small serial chunks finish inside
  the timeout and each one keeps the whole conversation in context.
  (`parallel_chunks = on` only pays off with `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL` raised.)

## Local-model tips

- Keep **locations** to one or two entries. The continuity pass asks the model to
  honour every location anchor in every scene, and a local model will obey too
  literally - cramming all of them into one shot.
- Give the performer a **name** in `extra_cast` ("Lead singer: Mara, ...").
  Without one the model invents a new name for them in each chunk.
- A 27B model at Q4 takes ~20-40 s per scene chunk. A 3-minute song is
  ~18 pieces, so budget 5-10 minutes for the writing pass.

nodes.title: Reference images
widgets_values:
# Reference images and multimodal models

`qwen3.8:27b` reports the **vision** capability, so the pictures you connect to the
writer's `image_1..image_9` really are sent to it - downscaled, as part of the
prompt - and it writes `<Picture 1>` bindings from what it can see.

The picture goes to **three** places, and all are needed:

1. the **H3 Characters** node's `image` - it travels with the cast line, and its `image`
   output feeds the **writer's** `image_1`, so the prompt describes the right face;
2. the **video node's** `ref_image_0` - so the renderer actually has the picture;
3. the **Prompt Preview**'s `image_1` - the thumbnail next to every scene.

The model is **ref2va** (`minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`) - the
picture-binding checkpoint; workflows without a picture run fl2va with `prompt_mode = FL / T2VA`.

`prompt_mode` is **Ref2VA**, the guide that binds `<Picture N>` labels.
`reference_image_use = Characters only` means a photo is a person, never a
location: its background is ignored unless an `image_notes` line says otherwise.

**If your model has no vision** (plain `qwen3`, `llama3.1`, `mistral`, most
"instruct" text models) the images cannot help it, and sending them errors out.
Use the text-only workflow instead - `h3_music_video_masked_audio_ollama_textonly.json`
- where `prompt_mode = FL / T2VA` and everything is written in words.

Check what a model can do: the **📏 Show 1024 tokens** modal tags every pulled
model with `vision` / `thinking` / `tools`, read from Ollama's own metadata.
